title: Consolidate identity crypto shims and modernize TLS/SAML stack
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Scope: replace brittle, service-specific crypto shims and multiple SAML/JWT libraries with a consolidated, auditable identity runtime surface. This ticket covers: (1) migrating our internal services from xmlsec-python bindings to a vetted native verifier (evaluate /proto: go-saml/native-saml), (2) upgrading OpenSSL across Linux builds to 3.2.x with FIPS-compatible build flags where required by Private deployments, (3) standardizing JWT/OAuth verification on the new jose-lite library and adding strict claim validation, and (4) ensuring our CI toolchain runs deterministic builds with bundled, signed ciphers to avoid transitive vuln drift.

Goals: remove ad-hoc per-service crypto patches, close CVE surface from transitive deps, provide an opt-in FIPS mode for Private customers, and create a migration path with non-disruptive rollback.

Non-goals: this ticket does not change SSO UX, nor does it rework higher-level provisioning flows (that will be follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: All runtime images build with OpenSSL 3.2.x and pass integration smoke tests (TLS handshake + token exchange)
SAML auth paths use the new verifier and unit tests cover assertion validation edge cases (clock skew, nested attributes, signing alg fallback)
JWT verification uses jose-lite with strict claim checks; existing tokens are validated and a deprecation window announced for older token formats
CI has a dependency-scan gate that fails on high/critical license or CVE findings for identity packages
Staged rollout configured with feature flag identity.crypto.runtime and automatic fallback to legacy adapter on verification errors
implementation_notes: Primary languages impacted: Go runtime service, Python SAML glue for legacy connectors
Build matrix: alpine-3.18 (glibc compat), debian-bullseye for on-prem packages
Backports: small compatibility shim for token parsers to accept existing JWT kid-less tokens during the deprecation window
CI: add openssl-verify.sh that asserts library symbol versions in resulting binaries
Performance: run KV cache microbenchmark because new verifier increases cold-start parsing cost ~7-12% — add lazy-load optimization if observed in canary
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: SAML verifier behavioral differences could break some corporate IdPs. Mitigation: ship as opt-in flag and run a 48-hour canary per tenant; maintain legacy adapter behind fallback policy.

Risk: OpenSSL ABI changes in 3.2 could affect native plugins. Mitigation: produce both legacy and 3.2 build artifacts, run smoke tests against both, and provide rolling upgrade doc for Dedicated/Private customers.
Risk: Token compatibility during rollout. Mitigation: support a hybrid verification path in gateway for 30 days and emit deprecation telemetry for tokens that require legacy path.
Risk: Increased container image size due to static linking. Mitigation: strip debug symbols and use multi-stage builds to keep final image small.
Compliance: FIPS mode requires additional validation steps; coordinate with security and legal for release notes and customer opt-in flow.
qa_checklist: Unit tests for jose-lite wrapper added and green
End-to-end tests: SAML login + attribute mapping for 3 different IdP samples (Okta, ADFS, AzureAD)
Load test: 10k auth validations/min to validate latency regression <15% on p3-small-equivalent
Canary rollout plan documented in Confluence with rollback steps
